title: Tikka masala
text: Marinate chicken in yoghurt and spices for at least two hours, grill it, then simmer the pieces in a tomato and cream sauce with garam masala.

title: Naan at home
text: A hot cast-iron pan works almost as well as a tandoor: roll the dough thin, cook it dry until it bubbles, then brush it with garlic butter.

title: Pour-over coffee
text: Use water just off the boil and a gooseneck kettle. Bloom the grounds for thirty seconds, then pour in slow circles until you reach the target weight.

title: Pour-over brewing guide
text: Heat water to just below boiling and pour it through a gooseneck kettle. Let the coffee bloom for half a minute before pouring slowly in circles up to your target weight.

title: Giraffe feeding
text: Giraffes browse acacia leaves high above other herbivores, using a prehensile tongue up to half a metre long to strip branches between the thorns.

title: Why zebras have stripes
text: The leading explanation is that stripes deter biting flies, which struggle to land on striped surfaces; camouflage and heat regulation are weaker hypotheses.

title: Savanna grazing
text: Zebras and giraffes often graze side by side because they eat different parts of the vegetation and share the work of spotting predators.

title: Coral reef ecosystems
text: Reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor but shelter roughly a quarter of all marine species, from tiny shrimp to reef sharks.

title: Public aquariums
text: Large aquarium tanks recreate reef habitats behind thick acrylic walls so visitors can watch schools of tropical fish swim past.

title: Tyre dumps
text: Discarded tyres pile up in illegal dumps, where they trap rainwater, breed mosquitoes and can burn for months, releasing toxic smoke.

title: Plastic waste
text: Most plastic ever produced has not been recycled; it sits in landfills or open dumps, or breaks down into microplastics in rivers and seas.

title: Most plastic is never recycled
text: The majority of all plastic made so far was never recycled. It ends up in landfill or open dumps, or fragments into microplastics in rivers and oceans.

title: Supermarket shelf placement
text: Brands pay for eye-level shelf space, while staples like rice and flour are placed low or at the back so shoppers walk past more products.

title: Fresh produce displays
text: Fruit is stacked in angled crates with price cards in front; oranges and pineapples are often displayed next to each other for colour contrast.

title: Corner shop stock
text: A small convenience store keeps snacks, instant noodles, sauces and tea on wooden shelves, with mugs and souvenirs on the top row.

title: Keepie-uppie drills
text: Juggling a football with your feet, thighs and head improves first touch and balance; beginners should let the ball bounce once between touches.

title: Cups and ball trick
text: In the classic shell game a ball is hidden under one of three cups, the cups are shuffled, and the audience must guess where the ball ended up.

title: Alphabet blocks
text: Wooden letter blocks help young children learn to spell short words by arranging the cubes in a row on the floor or a table.

title: Crowd density
text: Seen from above, pedestrians in a busy square spread out evenly until a performer or obstacle makes them cluster.

title: Oven safety
text: Never leave a gas oven on unattended, and keep kettles and pans away from the vents on top of an old freestanding cooker.

title: Flamenco guitar
text: Flamenco guitarists use rasgueado strumming and percussive golpe taps on the soundboard; the minera is a slow, dark palo from the mining towns of Murcia.

title: Royalty-free stock music
text: Upbeat corporate tracks with light percussion and piano are common background music for product videos and presentations.
